rule:
G4 (plan 5.1) evaluated from the saved samples, for every valid timed job whose times the report presents (no GPU;
records only).  Run as a script it writes tasks/T28/g4_activity.json; collect.py imports `evaluate()`.

Revision 3 (third check, D31).  Jobs: the fixed-state timing runs (ours T, released F), the released native runs N and
record runs R (k <= 160; R_k256 is invalid and its times are not results), and our matched-rule loops L.  Sections:
setup (a), released per-solve setup (b) and solve, our setup (b) and solve, and the design-loop solve and design step.

Activity.  Plan 5.1 G4: "the mean foreign 3D-engine use ... is sampled every <= 10 s over each timed section".  The
sampler is Get-Counter '\GPU Engine(*engtype_3D)\Utilization Percentage' at 5 s, and each value is the mean over the
interval since the previous sample, (t_{i-1}, t_i].  For a section [a, b] on the sampler's clock:
  - the covering intervals are those that overlap [a, b]; the section is covered when they contain [a, b];
  - the plan's measure is the duration-weighted mean over the covering intervals, classed ok (< 1 %), flagged
    (1-5 %) or excluded (> 5 %);
  - the strict bound is sum(f_i * dt_i) / duration: the counter is non-negative, so all foreign use inside the section
    lies inside the covering intervals.  A bound < 1 % proves "ok", 1-5 % proves "not excluded"; a bound > 5 % does
    not decide the 5 % rule ("unresolved"), it does not show interference.
Our processes (T, L) time their sections on the sampler's clock (time.time() in the same Windows process); the
envelope is the section widened by 0.1 s (the counter's reception lag is <= 9 ms, fix_r2/sampler_lag.json).  Our
setup (b) has no wall timestamps; it is evaluated over its envelope [end of memory pass, start of timed solve 0] with
the duration setup_b_s.
Released processes (F, N, R) time their sections on the WSL clock.  The offset between the WSL and Windows clocks
during a job is not known: fix_r2/wsl_clock_offset.json gives an empty interval for F_S1_k160 under a constant offset
and the 4 s pre-exit hold (D3), and a later reading cannot stand in for it.  Two tiers:
  - clock-free (decisive): every section of a job lies inside the job's own window [t_launch, t_exit] of
    runs/<job>/monitor.json, which is on the sampler's clock.  The section's strict bound is computed from the counter
    intervals that overlap that window.  It needs no clock alignment;
  - conditional: if the offset is constant during the job, it lies in [last WSL timestamp + hold - t_exit,
    t_prog0 - t_launch]; the section's envelope on the sampler's clock is [t0 - hi, t1 - lo], evaluated as above.
    Where that interval is empty, the condition is refuted by the records and the tier is "not available".
Revision 4 (fourth check, D34-D37).  (i) The strict bounds hold for the sections evaluated (whole solves, setups,
design steps), not for parts of them: `step_level()` bounds the 5 % rule at Krylov-step duration from the same
integral (released: the job window's; ours: the largest solve section's) divided by the median step.  (ii) The
record runs R time their design step in pieces that start after the untimed compliance transfer and dumps
(released/t28_driver.c:338-379), so [t_ret, t_ret + design_s] is not the timed interval: the conditional tier is
dropped for R's design steps; their clock-free bound needs only the duration and stays.  (iii) Limitation: the
sampler is one `Get-Counter -Continuous` call with a wildcard instance path, which resolves the matching process
instances once, when it starts.  Every bound here covers the instances enumerated then; the records neither establish
coverage of a process created later nor show that such a process interfered.
Clock.  A section of >= 1 s whose median SM clock is below 1500 MHz is "low clock" (plan 5.1).  Our T and L solve and
design windows carry their medians in the record; our setup sections have no saved clock series, so the rule is
undecidable for those of >= 1 s.  Released runs: the wrapper's 1-s nvidia-smi series (runs/<job>/t28_launch.json) is on
the sampler's clock, so the released section cannot be located in it exactly.  A median of n samples is low only if at
least ceil(n/2) of them are low, and not low only if at least ceil(n/2) are not low; a section of duration d holds at
least n_min = floor(d / g) samples, g the largest gap of the series.  Over a window W that surely contains the section
(the job window, or the conditional envelope): fewer than ceil(n_min/2) low samples in W proves "not low", fewer than
ceil(n_min/2) high samples proves "low"; otherwise "undecided".
limitation: the activity sampler is a single Get-Counter -Continuous call with a wildcard instance path ('\\GPU Engine(*engtype_3D)\\Utilization Percentage', drivers/t28lib.py:_PS_ACT), which resolves the matching process instances once, at its start. Every activity value and bound covers the process instances enumerated then. The records neither establish coverage of a process created later nor show that such a process interfered (D37)
